title: Active Customers View
statement:
A shop keeps its customers and their orders in two tables:

- `customers`: `id` (integer key), `name` (text, unique), and `city` (text).
- `orders`: `id` (integer key), `customer_id` (the customer who placed it), `total` (numeric), and `ordered_on` (date).

Create a view named `active_customers` with one row for each customer who has at least one order. It has two columns: `name` and `order_count`, the number of orders that customer placed. Customers with no orders are left out.

Then select `name` and `order_count` from the view, ordered by `name`. Creating the view prints the `CREATE VIEW` tag before the result.

Expected output:

```text
CREATE VIEW

     name     | order_count
--------------+-------------
 Amara Okafor |           3
 Chen Wei     |           2
 Elif Kaya    |           1
 Felix Wagner |           1
(4 rows)
```

hints: A view is a saved query: `CREATE VIEW name AS SELECT ...`.
Joining customers to orders keeps only customers who have a matching order. Then group by customer and count.

sql.solution:
CREATE VIEW active_customers AS
SELECT c.name, COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM customers AS c
JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name;

SELECT name, order_count
FROM active_customers
ORDER BY name;
